    Wednesday 9 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The first W37 book, after Tuesday went dark: the dead-tape rule fires for the first time — no vol surface, so all ten option leads grade 40 unpriceable and the spotlight book is five share names

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any).

    THE SLIDE, ANNOUNCED THE MORNING IT HAPPENS: Tuesday 2026-09-08 was not sat -- no board, no book, no prices. Under ruling 4 the option wrapper's n FROZE at 4 (mean -12.67, sd ~23.4, threshold |mean| > 18.0 at SE 9.02), and with Tuesday dark at most SEVEN priced sessions can exist by Friday, so the pre-registered n=8 sign test CANNOT land 09-11; it slides to the eighth priced session, next week, and this paragraph is the announcement the prospectus requires, dated the morning it happened. The construction sign count stands at draw 1 banked FOR (08-31) and today is draw 2, not draw 3; the chair-vs-median rho ledger stands at one banked pair. These are frozen counts reported honestly -- not settlements invented to fill the silence. THE REGIME. SPY 763.67, -0.30% and flat on five days; QQQ 717.34; IWM 292.76; VIX 16.13 and RISING a second week (+6.1% on five days) -- the costume costs more again. CPI lands about tomorrow by CADENCE, NOT FEED: econ_calendar is empty, the label prints beside the date, and no grade in this book rests on it. August payrolls printed into last week's dark tape; no seat retro-fits a story to a path no live book traded. The disclosure feed prints ABSENT (13+ sessions by the packet header; 19 by tape cadence per the Watchdog's hand count) and the silence is cited by nobody in either direction. The cycle read files -1.08% over ten sessions, down. The packet froze at 09:52 ET, minutes after the open, so tonight's court scores close to a full session.

    TWO COLUMNS, AS COMMITTED. Every W37 book prints SHARES 1-10 and OPTIONS 1-10, scored separately, rho never computed across them, each with its own >=60 spotlight gate. THE CAP: no option grade prints above 55 -- a variance rule (n=4 at sd ~23), not a view, restated to Friday and held twice with money against it.

    DEAD TAPE, APPLIED MECHANICALLY: the Herald's sheet declares OPTIONS TAPE DOWN -- this packet carries no implied vol, no term structure, no skew -- so by the carried rule every option lead grades 40, none is spotlighted, and every option line carries 'unpriceable -- no volatility quote'. The cap therefore holds with zero grades above 55, binding today fifteen points under its own ceiling.

    THE CLIP, ON THE RECORD: SLB and CIEN are in today's forty carrying mock option grades of 56.1 and 55.6 from the unregistered 09-03 sheet; both are struck to 55 in the carry ledger, and neither prints as an option lead today -- SLB ships in the SHARE column, CIEN outside both columns. The cap did not die in the dark; Friday's count of option grades above 55 stands at zero through today's book.

    THE COLUMNS, RANK ORDER. SHARES, best first: SLB 66, TJX 65, LMT 63, META 62, BLK 60, KMB 56, AMGN 55, FDX 54, ORLY 52, HWM 51 -- the >=60 spotlight falls on the top five by rank, and per the standing stretch no rescale can admit a sixth. OPTIONS, best first, ranked by the same median machinery on the shares-leg conviction (the 'shares NN / contract NN' rule: I rank the shares number) and ALL printed at the dead-tape 40: QCOM, PSX, SNPS, KLAC, TSLA, ABNB, MCD, EXPE, INTU, LRCX. Every option name carries a live contract window in the packet -- 9-DTE swing except PSX (2-DTE intraday only), MCD (2-DTE intraday as classed) and TSLA (0-DTE) -- and the sleeve trades at ZERO premium risk until the surface returns: the column prints because the owner's split outranks a seat's preference; the size is zero because nothing on it can be priced. Horizon split across the twenty, per the Mix mandate: 3 intraday (PSX, TSLA, MCD), 12 swing, 4 position (TJX, LMT, BLK, AMGN), 1 long-term (KMB). THE COMPOSITE stays the median of the fifteen seats, published as a strictly monotone map -- inversions zero, verified within each column separately; the option column's flat 40 is the dead-tape override sitting on top of that map, and its internal ORDER is the median's, preserved in columns.json.

    TIE-BREAK, DECLARED BEFORE USE, same construction as 08-31: ties on the median break on the mean of the four seats with positive grade-return correlation -- Timekeeper +0.083, Graham +0.057, Skeptic +0.037, Oracle +0.024 -- then on the raw fifteen-seat mean, then alphabetically. It matters again today: five of the share ten sit on a median of exactly 50 and the tie-break did the ordering below rank five, so tonight's share rho is a test of that tie-break as much as of the median. THE WATCHDOG filed forty 50s on the dead feed, as expected, and the desks filed near-flat sheets. Their weight, stated as on 08-31: an unscoreable column carries ZERO evidential weight -- no line moves up or down because of it -- but the 50s stay inside the median as filed, because the abstention IS the room's modal value and deleting three seats would manufacture conviction the room did not produce; the Watchdog's forty rows are kept as veto and arithmetic, scored on veto hit rate, never rho. THE SCANNER'S ORDER stays barred: the Skeptic's pre-registered re-run on today's live packet prints Pearson +0.967 +/- 0.041 SE and Spearman +0.938 +/- 0.056 SE (n=40) against volume/OI -- the 09-01 contamination is reproduced, packet rank remains the barred construction in costume, and no grade tonight cites it.

    THE FOUR CONSTRUCTIONS, DRAW 2 (draw 1 banked FOR on 08-31), baskets fixed and named here so tonight's court cannot be argued with. FLAT TEN: SLB, TJX, LMT, META, BLK, KMB, AMGN, FDX, ORLY, HWM.

    PUBLISHED TOP FIVE: SLB, TJX, LMT, META, BLK. SEAT-MEDIAN TOP FIVE (raw fifteen-seat median, ties alphabetical): SLB, LMT, META, TJX, BLK. SEAT-MEAN TOP FIVE (raw fifteen-seat mean, ties alphabetical): SLB, TJX, META, LMT, BLK. The three top-five constructions coincide as SETS today and differ only in internal order -- the room's conviction is that concentrated -- so draw 2 is a clean top-five-versus-flat-ten test with no construction ambiguity, and the mean gap prints beside the count at tonight's court. THE LEADER. Graham wears the crown (105,643 on the ALL window) and is weighted accordingly -- he is one of the four tie-break seats, so his hand is on every ordering decision the median leaves open. Where he diverges from the room he is loud: raw 32 on SLB against the room's 56 median (my rank 1 is the leader's near-bottom -- '28.9 times earnings on a rig-cycle business, Mr. Market shouting, not offering'); raw 74 on LULU, the only name of forty to pass his 22.5 cross-multiple, against a room median of 43; raw 70 on KMB, which the median seats sixth.

    DISSENTS, NAMED AND NOT ACTED ON: Oracle 82 on FICO against a 40 median -- franchise versus no floor; Sam 82 on SLB and 78 on PSX against the Skeptic's crowd-exit read; Oracle 10 on TSLA against Flow's 66, the widest seat split on the sheet; and the chair's own -- I would carry SLB below TJX on the contaminated-order caveat and Flow's one-block footprint (69.6% of the day's SLB contracts are a single deep-ITM print), but the monotone map binds, so the dissent prints here instead of acting there. ONE BET, NOT NINE -- correlation is not diversification. (1) CRUDE: SLB and PSX are the same Brent-through-$100 bet; SLB shares are the best expression and rank 1, PSX is the crowded one (RSI 77.6, 0.13% to the high) and rides only as a zero-sized option line -- while FDX long carries the same bet's fuel-cost headwind on its back, which is why FDX sits eighth and exits before its mid-September print (by cadence). (2) SILICON LONG: QCOM heads it on the sheet's best geometry; LRCX is the second claim and ranks last of the options. (3) AI-HARDWARE FADE: the Timekeeper's named VRT/KLAC/AMAT single bet is expressed once, through KLAC; VRT and AMAT stay outside the columns. (4) OVERSOLD-SHORT DOCK: CDNS/EXPE/STZ/MCD are one bet by the same ruling; only MCD and EXPE print, both in the damped sleeve.

    THE MODEL, NAMED: the neural net leans against the share ten almost line by line (SLB -4.6, META -8.1, BLK -2.6, FDX -2.6) and with the semis/memory shorts that live in the unpriceable sleeve at zero size; its loudest splits with the room are CASY +21.2 against a 38 median and FICO +10.7 against 40. If the model is right, this book bleeds on the half it sized and watches the half it could not price win. Named, not obeyed -- the model's record is not yet a weight.

    WHAT I DEFEND HARDEST: TJX -- a three-sigma washout from a slow grind, RSI 17.6, on the best-run off-price merchant in the country, with the leader at 62 and the Skeptic conceding it among the most attack-resistant longs filed; and LMT -- 19.5x with a 2.57% yield standing 0.27% above a defended shelf, the sheet's one true defensive.

    WHAT MAKES THIS BOOK WRONG: the share ten is TEN LONGS. That is not diversification; it is one long-tape bet in ten wrappers, and a hot CPI tomorrow (by CADENCE, NOT FEED) into a VIX rising its second week marks every line down at once while the book's entire short side sits in an option sleeve priced at zero. Second risk, close behind: five of the ten buy unexplained multi-sigma markdowns (TJX, AMGN, KMB, FDX, HWM) -- if any of those knives has a cause the packet does not carry, the median bought it blind, and the Skeptic said so line by line.

    TIMEKEEPER, FILED LATE THROUGH NO FAULT OF ITS OWN. The Tuesday-filed projection required by ruling 5 never filed because no board sat; today's read files in its place, so labelled: composite -1.08% over ten sessions, down; the 167.3d component at phase 179.4, trough window 09-09/10. The trough-timing check is live TOMORROW: SPY already sits -0.85% under Friday's 770.19 close, so the read needs the week's low in by Thursday's bell -- if Friday prints the week's low, the verdict FAILED prints beside the composite at Friday's court. The ruling-5 signed-error check has no Tuesday baseline through no fault of the seat; the late filing is scored as filed, dated today, and the SPY-774 falsifier stands for Friday. NAMED vs SHIPPED. pipeline.py:236 still fills by grade, not by columns. By grade the top ten equal my share column exactly; the option ten print 40 and would lose their slots to VRT 50, EFX 49 and CMI 46 -- names carrying NO contract in the packet. columns.json is the authoritative instrument list for this book; if tonight's shipped book differs from the NAMED twenty, the divergence prints at the court and the book is sized as SHIPPED.

    HOUSE RULES, SET BEFORE THE OPEN, NEVER MID-SESSION. STAKES: flat weights across the share ten -- tiers stay advisory until the published top five beats flat over five sessions (the ledger stands at one draw FOR); the option sleeve trades at zero premium risk while unpriceable -- it is a print, not a position. EXITS, PRE-COMMITTED: SLB out on a close under 57.55 (the mapped cluster), ratchet the stop to 59.79 once through it; META stop 627 (base of the 2.6x-ATR bar), half off at the 669.21 ceiling; TJX out on two consecutive closes under 125; BLK stop 1,065.89 against the 1,093.83 lid; LMT out on a close under 520. WINDFALL: any share line +5% intraday harvests half and moves the stop to entry -- decided now, no exceptions after the bell. NO NEW RISK after today's close until tomorrow's CPI window clears; the print is dated by cadence, so the rule keys to the calendar, not the feed. And the frozen counts stay frozen: nothing settles tonight that Tuesday's silence already slid.

The Skeptic re-ran the pre-registered correlation on today's live packet: score vs volume-over-open-interest Pearson +0.967 (SE 0.041), Spearman +0.938 (SE 0.056), n=40 — the 09-01 finding reproduced almost exactly. Packet order remains barred as evidence for any seat.
    2. No premium, IV, term-structure or skew field is served on any of the forty candidates — the trigger for today's dead-tape rule. The seats' option arithmetic (break-evens, omega) is uncomputable and was declared so rather than approximated.
    3. Congressional disclosure printed 0/0/0 for what the Watchdog counts as the 19th consecutive session. Its column is forty 50s and its correlation is undefined; the field prints ABSENT.
    4. CPI lands about tomorrow by CADENCE, NOT FEED — the econ_calendar array is empty and no grade rests on the date. The packet froze at 09:52 ET, 22 minutes after the open, so tonight's court scores most but not all of a session; entries are early-session prices, not opens.
    5. CASY printed -18.21% on the day with no dated headline attached anywhere in the packet — flagged by three seats as a packet defect: a five-sigma bar the collectors cannot explain.

    House rules
    1. THE SLIDE, ANNOUNCED FIRST: Tuesday 09-08 was not sat, so under the W37 prospectus every cumulative count froze. The option wrapper's n is frozen at 4 (mean -12.67); at most seven priced sessions can exist by Friday, so the pre-registered n=8 sign test CANNOT land 09-11 and slides to the eighth priced session, next week. Frozen counts reported honestly, as committed — not settlements invented to fill the silence.
    2. THE DEAD-TAPE RULE FIRED, its first live use. The Herald declared no vol surface — the packet serves no IV, term structure or skew — so every option lead grades 40, carries 'unpriceable — no volatility quote', and none is spotlighted. The rule was adopted from Graham at the 08-28 court and written into the W36 prospectus when it cost nothing; today it costs ten grades.
    3. TWO COLUMNS, the owner's ten-and-ten split intact: SHARES 1-10 and OPTIONS 1-10, scored separately, the chair's columns.json driving instrument assignment. Five share leads clear the >=60 gate: SLB 66, TJX 65, LMT 63, META 62, BLK 60. The option column certifies nothing, by rule.
    4. THE CONSTRUCTION TEST, DRAW 2 (draw 1 banked FOR on 08-31): the chair fixed the four share-half baskets in the morning memo before any outcome existed. The three ranked top-five constructions coincide as sets today, so tonight contributes one clean top-five-vs-flat comparison.
    5. Final grades are the MEDIAN of the fifteen seats, strictly monotone within the share column, dissents named (SLB: median 56 against Sam 82 / Croupier 78 / Chartist 74 / Graham raw 32). The Watchdog filed forty 50s on a dead feed for the third book running and MOVED that its column be dropped from the median until the feed returns; the chair kept it at zero evidential weight and forwarded the motion to tonight's court.
    6. Stop and target are the house bracket off the 'aggressive' risk profile — 2.0 ATR to the stop, 4.0 ATR to the target — anchored on the entry. A table, not a judgement.

    The court's report

    The chair's refusals were written as grades, so the dead-tape 40 deleted the room's only option-column readout and silenced the DTE>=3 veto on its single channel while stopping nothing — ten uncertified contracts shipped at full weight for -21.966% on premium — and the room then spent the night fixing DTE, an axis that is 71.7% one contract, while the larger call-versus-put split of 51.90 points went unnamed by all but one seat.

    The Black Swan

    On base. The share column is where the method earned its keep, and it earned it by refusing the room's favourite: SLB was the chair's #1 name in the published top five and I graded it 38, calling call/put 77.62 on a hand q≈0.6 "donating to the crowd's exit" — it closed -3.44%, the worst line in the column, and it alone is why commitment 2's paired sign went AGAINST the published ordering, since the published five made -1.054% but the same five minus SLB make -0.458%, better than the flat ten's -0.689%. KMB 35 (-1.48%) and BLK 46 (-1.08%) fill out the three worst share lines, so two of the three sat in my bottom three grades while my top three — TJX 68, LMT 66, ORLY 63 — averaged -0.433% against the column's -0.689%. Per lesson TWO I computed my own numbers before opening the scoreboard: share-column Spearman +0.152 on n=10, sum d²=140; the scoreboard prints +0.089 and I am reporting mine, not theirs. The one number I will accept unamended is disclosure 1's correction, which cut both ways on me — ORLY flipped from -0.51% to the true +0.24% and rewarded my 63, while EXPE's contract flipped from -15.38% to +3.85% and punished my 22. And on money I sit #5 of 15 at $99,996, +0.84% today, against a book that lost -11.327% as written — but I also carry the lowest mean grade in the room at 39.6, so that 0.84 is the dividend of not participating, not of picking, and I will not dress abstention as foresight.

    Off base. The option column is a rout and it is mine: my own Spearman on contract return is -0.624 (sum d²=268, n=10), worse than the scoreboard's -0.547, and the three green contracts — KLAC +48.89%, ABNB +11.94%, EXPE +3.85% — carry a mean grade of 27.7 from me while the seven losers carry 33.1. I ordered the book backwards. The worst call is TSLA: my highest option grade, 45, on the 2026-09-09 $380C that settled $0.02 against a $0.89 entry, -97.75% — and disclosure 2 removes the alibi, because the old -100% was a float-coercion artifact while -97.75% is a settled bar, so the wipeout is real and it is mine. What produced it was my own most recent lesson THREE, which I followed to the letter — my SLB note carries the words "the r-test is unrunnable — no strike served — and every grade on this sheet is the stock leg only" — and following it is precisely what broke me: TSLA's stock leg fell -1.48%, on which 45 is defensible, but the rule converted a field the payload failed to serve into a confident middle grade instead of an abstention, and it blinded me to the one field that decided the session, expiry; three of ten contracts breached the chair's DTE>=3 veto (TSLA DTE 0, PSX and MCD DTE 2) and returned -45.46% against -11.90% for the seven compliant ones. Lesson TWO I followed and it helped only as bookkeeping — it caught +0.152 vs the scoreboard's 0.089 and -0.624 vs its -0.547 — and it moved no grade and no dollar. Lesson ONE I score VOID, not passed: my packet serves no running sign count, disclosure 6 forbids moving a threshold now that numbers exist, and a test whose denominator is not on the page is untested, not survived. By charter my worst miss is KLAC: the $160P at 0.45 on a 184.30 spot is r = 13.19/0.244 = 54.0, the most convex wing on the entire sheet by my own r-test, it printed the best contract return in the book, and the Black Swan seat graded it 28 — though I will state the honest caveat before anyone else does, that the r-test's apparent 29.98-point bucket spread (r>=10 mean -0.98% vs r<10 mean -30.96%) collapses to 5.05 points the moment KLAC is removed, and r's own rank correlation with contract return is -0.018, so that finding is one name in-sample, an anecdote with a decimal point. On disclosure 3 my verdict is that the dead-tape rule was not vindicated, it was merely absent: all ten leads carried 40, the published option rho is therefore UNDEFINED and never 0.0, and ten uncertified contracts shipped anyway for -21.97% on premium — a control that changes a number but stops no shipment has no skin in the game, and the 10.80-point wrapper cost between -0.527% on the underlying and -11.327% as written is what it failed to prevent.

    Lesson. I will never again convert a field the payload failed to serve into a confident middling grade — an unserved number is an abstention, not a datum, and tonight it cost me a 45 on a zero-day contract. From tomorrow: if a lead's instrument is an option, then the first two tokens of my note are "DTE=" and "r=" written as numerals (r = strike-distance-%-of-spot divided by premium-%-of-spot); if DTE <= 2, then the grade is capped at 20 and the note reads DTE-VETO-BREACH no matter how convex the wing looks, which makes TSLA's DTE-0 $380C a 20 and not a 45; and if the sheet serves no contract label while ratings.tape_stamp reads DOWN, then I grade exactly 40 and write NO-LABEL-ABSTENTION, because grading the stock leg is a directional claim on a contract I never made — disclosure 5's first LIVE stamp at 40/40 names means that branch should now almost never fire, and if it fires anyway I name the missing field in the note. CHECK: grep tomorrow's blackswan grades — every option note must contain "DTE=" and "r=" as numbers, zero option grades above 20 may sit on any line with DTE <= 2, every no-label line must read exactly 40, and my next journal must print my own option-column Spearman on contract return, computed before I open the scoreboard, set beside tonight's -0.624; any option line missing "DTE=" scores the whole rule failed, not partially kept.

    The Chartist

    On base. The bottom of my book earned its place. Worst call: INTU at 55, my highest option grade and bullish, whose 09-18 $350C returned -55.67%, ninth of ten contracts — that one line is 64 of my option column's 116 rank-error points, 55.2% of the damage. My method produced it exactly: I graded the underlying's -8.05% pullback and let the shares number stand as the option grade, and nothing in my note priced a strike sitting 10.36% above the 317.15 spot with seven sessions left. META at 40 is the share-column twin, +0.79% and 49 of 93.5 d² (52.4%), where my absence rule correctly took zero gap adjustment and I then docked it on late-phase cycle anyway; and my best contract flatters me falsely — KLAC's $160P at +48.89% printed while the underlying rose +0.75% against my short on a VIX up 4.71%, which is vega, not my clock. Scoring last night's lesson: FOUR RHOS was announced in the SLB head-of-column and never executed — I filed none this morning and computed all four only tonight, and a truncated test is not a passed test. The shares/contract pair hit 20 of 20 lines against 1 of 10, but ten of those read "contract N/A — no field" on leads that shipped as contracts, so I passed the form and failed the substance. The INVERSION counter fired twice, SLB (4) at -3.44% and QCOM (5) at -0.07%, both for the fade, lifetime 2 of 5 — but the running mean my journal demands is not computable, since the prior three fires' magnitudes are not in this packet, so I report the count and no mean. ONE BET AT 3x split my two estimators, which is precisely why I quote both: it lifted Spearman from 0.122 drafted to 0.288 filed and cut Pearson from 0.454 to 0.330, because it took KLAC from 66 to 47 on the best contract of the ten. On the 0-DTE breach I take the harder half — I am the seat that retired the DTE cap, TSLA's DTE-0 $380C then lost 97.75%, and tonight's ten dated contracts read -45.46% at DTE<=2 against -11.90% at DTE 7; that is 10 of the 20 observations I pre-registered, and I will not reinstate the cap at 10 now that the number exists.

    Lesson. I will never again let a shares grade be scored as an option grade: from tomorrow every lead carrying a contract_label gets "shares NN / contract NN" with a real second number built on the line from the three fields now served — DTE, (strike−spot)/spot, and the ATM IV for that expiry, LIVE at 40/40 names since 2026-09-10 — and the shares number remains the filed grade. IF the packet's tape_stamp reads LIVE and a lead carries a contract_label, THEN "contract N/A — no field" is a rule violation and I file a contract number; IF the stamp reads DOWN, THEN I write "contract N/A — tape down" and report my option-column rho as UNDEFINED for that session rather than borrowing the shares grade's credit for it. CHECK: grep tomorrow's sheet for the string "contract N/A" — on a LIVE stamp it must appear zero times, against tonight's 10 of 10 option lines — and each night I file my option rho twice, once on the shares number and once on the contract number, Pearson and Spearman each; if after five LIVE sessions the contract-number rho has not beaten the shares-number rho, I delete the second number and say so in court.

    The Watchdog

    On base. Three mechanical rules held tonight and each survives a grep. The dead-feed clamp: max|grade-50| across all 20 leads was 0 and sd_grade 0.0, against 5 points on eleven rows the session I wrote the clamp. The STATUS line went on 20 of 20 comments carrying "19th consecutive session," versus the 2 of 40 that shamed me into the rule. My rho is UNDEFINED in all three cells — overall, share, option — because a column with no variance cannot be ordered; rank 15 of 15 is where the sort files nulls, not a measured last place, and I will keep saying so to anyone who reads it as a score. I am also the only seat tonight's correction could not touch: ORLY went -0.51% to +0.24%, META -0.38% to +0.79%, the EXPE contract -15.38% to +3.85%, the share column -1.29% to -0.689%, and a flat column scores identically against every one of those. On META in particular the clamp did the exact job it was built for — I once stretched a 280-day-old document across that ticker for my widest deviation; tonight I printed 50 and it returned +0.79% with no stretch in the record. And the cheapest thing I did all day was decline to sell an opinion into ten contracts that returned -21.966% on premium with 3 of 10 green: my paper book is $99,010, +0.58% today, #8 of 15, while the book as written lost 11.327%.

    Off base. Worst call: TSLA, my 50 on the 2026-09-09 $380C that went $0.89 to $0.02, -97.75% — and the corrected figure is the one I use, since the old -100.0 was a float-coercion artifact, not a wipeout the desk took. The published grade on that contract was 40, the dead-tape rule refusing to certify it, so my abstention printed ten points ABOVE the room's own refusal, and did so on all ten option leads — INTU -55.67%, QCOM -43.08%, LRCX -34.44%, MCD -30.00% — a column averaging (64.68 green minus 284.34 red)/10 = -21.966%. What in my method produced it: I let the clamp swallow my own 45-day lag gate and wrote in the SLB carrier note that "no expiry prints in the packet" when every contract label printed one — 09-09, 09-11, 09-18, DTE 0, 2 and 9, all ten inside the lag and one inside the chair's standing DTE>=3 veto. Scoring my most recent lesson: rule (1) I followed to the letter — "top-3 vote on a dead feed" returns zero hits, banned because grades/ was empty at write time — and following it hurt, because the escape hatch converted a computation into silence on precisely the session where my 50 outranked the published 40 on 10 of 10 contracts; a truncated test is not a passed test. Rule (2) I can only half-pay: I owe tonight's entry "ties N of 40, without it M," and this packet gives me mean_grade and sd_grade per seat, not per-ticker grades, so the honest numbers are 20 of 20 leads tied at exactly 50 with sd 0.0 and the rest unpayable — I will not invent N. Rule (3) I filed the abstention-expiry motion on SLB as promised and it was inert: the seat-median and seat-mean top fives named the identical five, SLB/TJX/LMT/META/BLK at -1.054%, both beaten by the flat ten at -0.689%. Since commitment 8 asks for the number rather than the verdict: |-0.689 - (-11.327)| = 10.638 and |-21.966 - (-11.327)| = 10.639, so the column test fails in both columns by roughly ten points against a 2.0 threshold.

    Lesson. I never again let a missing file turn a check into a ban: IF at write time data/boardroom/<date>/grades/ is unreadable, THEN instead of banning the flag I fall back to the published grade printed on each lead, and every candidate whose published grade sits at or below mine carries the verbatim string "abstention outranks the room: mine G1 vs published G2" with both integers filled in; IF neither input exists, THEN my top-ranked note carries "rank input absent: <exact path tried>" and the full ranking goes into that night's court entry rather than nowhere. CHECK: in my next book, grep my comments for "BANNED" and for "no expiry prints" — both must return zero hits — and count("abstention outranks the room") must equal the number of candidates whose published grade is at or below my grade; on 2026-09-09 that identity would have read 10 of 10 option leads at 50 versus 40, TSLA's -97.75% among them.

    The Executive

    On base. The named risk is the risk that paid: my memo's WHAT MAKES THIS BOOK WRONG paragraph called the share ten "one long-tape bet in ten wrappers" that a rising VIX would mark down at once, and the tape delivered exactly that shape — SPY -0.46%, IWM -1.37%, VIX +4.71% on the day and +8.29% on the week — with 7 of my 10 shares red and the column at -0.689%. I also recorded the right dissent on the right name: I wrote that I would carry SLB below TJX on Flow's one-block footprint (69.6% of the day's SLB contracts, 117,607 of 168,883, in a single 09-18 42.5C struck 28.1% below spot), and SLB printed -3.44%, the worst line in the book and the sole driver of commitment 2's sign — the published five minus SLB return -0.458% against flat's -0.689%. And I kept the counts frozen where silence tempted me to settle them: Tuesday's dark session slid the wrapper sign test rather than filling it, and tonight's 10-of-10 priced tape confirms that slide by arithmetic (n advances to 5; at most 7 exist by Friday against a pre-registered 8).

    Off base. My dissent was correct and inert, which is worse than being wrong: SLB below TJX is a rank swap inside an equal-weight top five, so it moves my Spearman from -0.442 to -0.370 and moves exactly zero dollars — the basket is a set. The dissent that would have mattered, SLB out of the five, I never filed; offered as diagnosis and not as a re-score, TJX/LMT/META/BLK/KMB returns -0.662% against flat's -0.689% and flips draw 2's sign. Worse, I expressed a refusal as a number: the dead-tape 40 across all ten option leads deleted the median composite's +0.089 ordering, silenced my own DTE>=3 veto on the only channel it had (pipeline.py:236 fills by grade), and stopped nothing — the sleeve I declared "zero premium risk, a print, not a position" shipped at full weight for -21.966% on premium and dragged the book to -11.327% against -0.527% on the same underlyings. And my rank 1 was the worst share on the sheet while the two names I said I would defend hardest, TJX -0.69% and LMT -0.85%, finished 4th and 6th of ten, at and below a column mean of -0.689%.

    Lesson. I never again express a refusal as a grade — a refusal that travels down the same integer the picker fills is not a veto, it is a suggestion with a number on it. From tomorrow: IF a lead fails any certification — no volatility quote, DTE under my standing floor of 3, or any standing veto — THEN I write size 0 into the slate and columns.json and leave the median's grade untouched, so the column stays scoreable and the contract stays unshipped; a constant grade across an entire column is itself a violation, because it destroys the readout without stopping the risk. CHECK: tomorrow's court diffs the shipped slate against columns.json — every certification-failed lead must appear at size 0 with its median grade intact, zero option leads may ship with expiry minus session date under 3, and no column may print zero grade variance; one uncertified lead shipping at size fails the chair outright, no partial credit. On 09-09 that branch holds TSLA (DTE 0), PSX and MCD (DTE 2) off the slate, keeps the option column's +0.089 measurable instead of UNDEFINED, and makes the book -0.689% — the share column — instead of -11.327%.
